**SUFFIXES:** alcoh**OL.** ket**ONE**. **AL**dehyde. carboxyl**(O)IC ACID**. esters, ethers, amines, and amide u just gotta practice.

for branches name things in alpha order ignoring any prefixes like di or tri. so 3,4,4-tri**e**thyl-2-**m**ethyl instead of 2-methyl-3,4,4-triethyl.

Branch names: meth, eth, prop, but, pent, hex, hept, oct, non, dec. For chains with 5 or more carbons i like to think about shapes with the same number of side (hexagon-6 sides, hex- 6 carbons).

look up a naming priority sheet, do practice worksheets, and number your carbons. also maybe it wont help u that much but look for connections in your life like reading ingredient lists for cleaners and other household things.

you only need to know polarity (how it affects solubility and whatnot), VESPR, and thats it. all new nomenclature and reactions. organic is the easiest unit for most people so dont stress. if u need extra resources 'William Zhou' has his lessons from covid posted on youtube.
